pairs.subject: transactions-over-a-replicated-log
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:3725 The pipeline store writes straight to a local better-sqlite3 engine inside its own IMMEDIATE transaction, with no consensus log, replicated state machine or apply step under it; a search of app/_lib/db/ for consensus, quorum, replicat and appliedIndex found nothing, so the subject's precondition (writes go through a replicated log) does not hold, and snapshot-read-plus-verify-log's own exclusion applies ('where the store is not replicated at all ... the ordinary transaction').

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:3588 A single-node analog: the decision is made outside the tx and re-verified under the writer lock, but there is no consensus round trip, verify list or log entry; the technique excludes non-replicated stores.
app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:3603 The conflict is a column-value CAS in a local SQLite tx, not a hash verification at replicated apply; no sentinel taxonomy for log commits applies.
app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:3727 No log index or modified-since fast path exists; the tx takes the local engine's write lock at BEGIN.
app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:3725 There is no log for a read-only transaction to stay out of; commits go to the local file.
app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:3725 No list verification hash is shipped anywhere; locking the SQLite writer covers the prefix reads.
app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:3727 One engine, with no cache, view or encoding wrapper stack around a transactional storage interface in this context.
app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:3727 No consensus library and no snapshot or log-truncation hooks; the store is a plain SQLite file.

pairs.registryProposal: The golden path's use_when trigger 'read-then-write handlers race and the last writer silently wins' carries no replication qualifier, so the mapper attaches this subject to single-node SQLite repositories. Those belong to data-access/concurrency-guards. The subject's first law (never hold the writer across a slow round trip; re-verify at write) does generalize to an LLM or subprocess hop on one node, and actOnPipelineEntry's expectedStage CAS is exactly that shape. Consider stating that generalization in a neighbour subject and narrowing this trigger to 'on a store whose writes go through a consensus log'.
